title: Claim binding
description: One student's binding of a GitHub account to an institutional email address, at students/claims/<github_id>.json in the private control repository. Written by acceptance/accept.mjs from lib/claim.mjs's buildClaimRecord. ORG-SCOPED, not per assignment: claim once and every later assignment in that organization recognises the account. Keyed by github_id because it is immutable and survives a username change, and one file per student because acceptance is concurrent and serialized only per login - two claims at once would collide on a single shared file. PRIVATE: this record must never reach Pages, which pages/scan.mjs enforces on both the address (the email-address content rule) and the record's own field names (claim-record-field, identity-field).

github_login.description: Display only, and refreshed on a later acceptance. The binding is on github_id; a student who renames on GitHub keeps their claim.

github_id.description: The immutable account id, and the filename. The sealed claim payload carries this too, and the hub refuses it when it does not match the issue author - a ciphertext lifted out of the public event archive would otherwise replay for anyone.

email.description: The claimed address, normalized by lib/claim.mjs's normalizeEmail (trim + lowercase, and nothing cleverer - a PXL address is not a Gmail address, so dots and +tags are significant).

domain_allowed.description: Whether the address was inside claim_domains. Always true under roster_mode: claim, where a failing domain is refused before any record is written. It exists for `open`, where nothing about the claim refuses and the answer is recorded rather than enforced - written on both so a consumer never has to know which mode produced the file.

claim_verified.description: True when the student picked an address GitHub had already verified on their account. EVIDENCE, NOT ENFORCEMENT: the hub cannot check it, because an installation token cannot read a user's email addresses - the same wall that withdrew roster_mode: org_member - so anyone opening the acceptance issue by hand can assert it. Its value is that the ordinary path records it truthfully, which makes a cohort review far sharper than 'does this address look like one of my students'.

student_number.description: Carried across from the matched roster entry under roster_mode: claim. Null under `open`, where there may be no roster to match against - GitHub never learns a student number, and inventing one would collide with real SIS numbering.

claimed_via.description: The assignment whose acceptance produced the binding. The binding itself is org-scoped; this records where it came from.

replaces.description: The binding this one replaced, when the student confirmed again because their earlier address no longer met the rules (lib/claim.mjs `bindingMeetsRules` - a `12345678@` address once deployment.yml asks for `firstname.lastname@`). Kept so the history of who this account said it was survives the rewrite, and so the roster can follow a row whose address came from the replaced claim. Absent on a first binding.

history.description: Every earlier binding of this account, oldest first, at most 20 - `replaces` is only the last one. Read for WHO WAS FIRST to hold an address (acceptance/accept.mjs `holdersOf`): an account that corrected away from an address and back keeps the time it first held it, rather than losing to whoever confirmed the address in between. Absent on a first binding.
